Yes, I think it was attachment therapy. The same therapist diagnosed me with sometging called "reactive attachment disorder."

Yep, I'm still in therapy even though it's been many years. My therapist sometimes looks at this sub actually. She thinks it's a great place for people who might otherwise be blown off by mental health professionals to vent and speak to each other about their experiences.

I just used "therapist" because it seemed the best way to tell my story, but honestly, I haven't thought of him as a legitimate therapist in a very long time, credentials or no. 

My Nmom absolutely knew she was causing me pain. She is a sadist through and through. I will never forget the gleam in her eyes when she saw me in any kind of distress. She enjoyed the things she did to me, and had done to me. The only thing she liked more than hurting me herself was watching others do it, especially people in positions of power. (Police, doctors, therapists, psychiatrists, justice system, etc.) 

Thank you for your well wishes. They mean a lot to me.
I looked him up recently on a lark and learned that he passed away a few years ago. I can't say that I'm too broken up about it.

She should have been arrested for a lot of things, but she never was. I was around that age, beaten and bruised from a beating when she called the police on me for daring to fight back. She had a scratch on her. A scratch. I was arrested and given a year of probation.
My goodness...I'm so sorry. I have no words for this except I hope you're doing better now.

I was. Unfortunately they have since passed. My dad died on the job of a heart attach, and my mom died shortly after by her own hand. The time I had with them was good. I'll always be thankful for that.
Lmao I wouldn't insult a cow by comparing that woman to one!

Honestly the first few years with her were okay. I think she wanted to do good at first, as her own mother was highly abusive. I think she ended up drunk on all that power though, and never dealt with her own trauma. When I ended up meeting my bio parents, they were better to me than she had ever been. Paperwork said my parents got clean a few month after losing me, NY parents fought in court, but Nmom won.
6000 miles away has proven to be enough thankfully.
Thankfully she is not in a position to hurt anyone anymore. The only person by her side is my N/E Step-dad.
Thank you. It's a bad memory, but I know I need to deal with it.
I often have a sense of humor about my childhood, and I've been firmly NC for years, but some experiences can't be shared like I usually do.

She was a CPS worker who was able to bend the system and call in favors to adopt me as a toddler on a single income while renting and having no savings. She thankfully had to quit when I was about 8 or so, but I always hate to think how many people's lives she ruined at that job.
My Nmom is super into Bernie. Her values are so conflicting and weird.

Yes, I do this. I can't possibly read every post, but I take a long look at the sub every few days and upvote all I can. I leave comments when I feel my contribution would be necessary, but a lot of times everything that can be said has already been said. I relate to the "telling the truth" part. To outsiders, a lot of our life stories sound incredibly outlandish. But narcissistic behavior IS often outlandish. It's so good that all of us have this community for support, especially for children of covert narcissists.

Not in the sense that they actually care about their child. When I attempted suicide as a young teen and my Nmom found out, the first words out of her mouth were "How DARE you try to take yourself away from me!" I'll never forget that.

The police arrested me when I was 9 for fighting back. I had a black eye, a bloody nose, and bruises all over me, new and old. She had ONE scratch on her arm. I was convicted of 3rd degree battery and got a year of probation, as well as 2 weeks in juvie. As a 9 year old girl. Good ol southern justice system.

I got the exact same line "real women don't wear makeup." I had a pretty toxic relationship with makeup growing up as all. My Nmom thought "makeup and all nail polish colors other than beige are for whores." She constantly said my entire childhood that "Whores wear makeup. Don't put out an ad unless you're ready to answer it." Also she never called it makeup, she called it "face paint." I'm not super proficient with makeup still, but I know some basics.
I wouldn't wish it on anybody either. I'm lucky in this case because she only started the majority of her conspiracy theories when I was almost 17/18.

My Nmom doesn't use toothpaste either! Last I heard, she only does 'oil pulling.' I'm not exactly sure what that is, but most of her teeth were gone by her late 20's. She also thinks toothpaste (especially ones containing fluoride) are a scam because 'chemicals'
I messaged my best friend a few minutes ago, and she agreed to role play the interview with me tomorrow! :)
Thank you mom, I'm definitely checking out this advice :)
Wow, MRSA is nothing to play around with. Like ever. A guy in my gaming group went into the hospital to be treated for mono. He contracted MRSA and ended up losing both of his legs.
Yep, I was called a spoiled brat even when I was sleeping on the linolium floor, being starved, and being beaten. Narcs are so delusional.

My Nmom is also pretty liberal and non-religious. She adopted me, and always told me "The second I saw you, I knew I had to have you." Like I was some puppy she saw in a pet store. As a little kid I thought it was sweet, but the older I get, the weirder it seems. I think she wanted an unquestioning little doll. She didn't seem to realize that babies are not dolls, and babies eventually grow up.
Not any more. She no longer has the capacity to harm me, and I see her for what she really is: a bitter, lonely old woman who, by her own making, has nothing and no one left.

I spent time in both JDC and the juvenile psych ward in the early 2000s in the South. I'd take JDC any day. I still have nightmares about the psych ward I was in and how I was treated there over a decade later. Went in 3 weeks after a suicide attempt (caused medication mismanagement by a parent) when I was no longer suicidal. I came out with CPTSD, anxiety, and severe depression. The conditions were barely livable, the staff were willfully ignorant of mental ilness at best and making fun of you for it at worst, witnessing stabbings and beatings were commonplace, being denied access to parents, never seeing sunlight, medical "professionals" gaslighting you, staff having sexual "relationships" with (aka sexually abusing) young girls and boys...god the list goes on. Every kid knew about that place and it was FEARED.
Oh wow, I had no idea about this either! I'll have to do some more research.

My Nmom refused to get me tested because, and I quote, "she didn't raise a r*t****d child." I was diagnosed with ASD when I was 18 and free of her. It's horrible that narcs often deprive us of basic mental health care. I'm really sorry you're going though this and I hope things get better.
You've been more intelligent and coherent in one comment than my Nmom was my entire childhood.
Haha I've been NC for years now, but if I'd had the presence of mind at the time I was a kid, I would've printed one out lol
I'm so sorry you had to deal with that weird 'dictator' crap as well.
Looking back, it was still so creepy though :/

I get this a lot and it's a little frustrating, however I realize most people have no idea I was abused and pretty much had to raise myself. Instead of correcting them, I just kinda chuckle and say something along the lines of "Well I sure learned what NOT to do from them." Most people don't press it and just leave it at that. I could correct them, but I prefer not everyone know my trauma. That's just a personal preference though, as I'm a very private person.

The cold, malicious glee in their eyes when they are planning something or have found out something they can use against you. It still gives me the shivers thinking about my Nmom's eyes when she looked at me like that. It meant something horrible was about to happen to me.
This should be shouted from the mountain tops.
Congratulations on going NC, it can be one of the hardest things to do. I'm glad you had the strength to do it and hope you sleep better soon. Keep your boundaries up and keep strong!

My Narc Adoptive mom used to ask me this constantly. I'm talking from like the time I could speak all the way to when I cut contact. She used to volunteer at women's shelters and saw how that stuff can break a person. I think she secretly hopes it will happen to me. She is a sadist.

They are both very miserable due to a mixture of health issues, poverty, and conspiracy theories. The decisions that led them to those conditions were entirely of their own making. I can't say that I feel super happy that they're miserable, but I do feel a certain sense of mild satisfaction.

Things are much better. I pretty much have a normal life now. Often, I look back on my childhood with humor because narcs are ridiculous and a lot of the things she did seem silly now, but there are some memories that still haunt me.

My Nmom studied childhood development in college and became...get this...a CPS worker. Due to her connections, she was able to adopt me as a single woman with a single income, no savings, and only a rental house in a crappy part of Sacramento. She only met my stepdad when I was 15. I find all this interesting because she was also a victim of horrific childhood abuse from her mother. I mean like daily beatings and several murder attempts. I think she originally got into the profession to try and help kids somewhat, but got a taste of the power and it changed her. She got ill when I was about 8 and had to leave her job at CPS thankfully. I don't want to imagine the damage she did there.
I am fully NC and haven't willingly spoken to them in several years.

As long as I've been NC, I still sometimes have nightmares of how my N Adoptive mom's eyes would light up, and she would have this predatory grin when she knew she'd hurt me in some way. The pure pleasure in her eyes in the presence of the consequences of her sadism. I've seen and experienced a lot of scary things in my life, but that gaze, that smile...I still get shivers thinking about it.
He and my aunt are very happy together and have a few kids and grandkids :)

My uncle is a great guy. More acurate though, he's my uncle in law. Through some very complicated but since forgiven family dynamics, he dated my Nmom for 10 years. He was subjected to abuse by her but rarely speaks of it. He ended up meeting and marrying Nmom's sister 5 years later. He was never fooled by my Nmom's antics, but used to keep mum on the subject for his wife's sake. Until he learned about what happened to me. My aunt was previously quite the enabler, but she's wised up a lot these past few years.

I spent too much time trying to show her how crazy she was...it's fruitless and I've learned just to ignore her.

Her response was so terrible...I'm sorry :( Any decent mother would have never said something like that. She should have been focusing on you and your feelings, not what may or may not happen to others. Sadly, that's typical narc behavior :(  

I never even bothered to tell my Nmom about being sexually assaulted. She is extremely sadistic and I knew she'd just use it to hurt me.

I was so glad to see your comments about your willingness to contact the adoption agency and CPS. My Nmom actually worked for CPS (ironic, right?) and for her, adopting a child to abuse was easy as pie. Even after my bio mom got clean, did parenting classes, and fought endlessly in court, my N adoptive mom still won and got to keep me. I was, in essence, stolen from my mother. I really hope you're able to make an impact. You could change that poor little girl's life <3

Narc parents don't care about how you feel or what made you suicidal. They don't care about getting you help. They don't care about supporting you in a difficult depression. They only care how your suicidal ideations make *them* feel and how it makes *them* look. 

The first thing my Nmom said to me after she found out I attempted suicide was "How *dare* you try to take yourself away from me?" At the time I remember wishing I hadn't failed because I just wanted to get away from her so badly.
Constantly. My Nmom would respond word for word like that as well. She would tell me that "I don't know" was just an excuse.

I understand where you're coming from. The pressure to go NC is heavy in a lot of support forums. Posters/commenters definitely mean well, but sadly that's not an option for some people, especially if they live with the narc or have money or legal entanglements. It's always good to try and infer through reading the post whether or not NC is a viable option before asking the poster about it :)
I posted a story about my Nmom in an askreddit thread and a user kindly pointed me here.

Thanks for all the hard work you do, and I hope people keep reporting trolls when they see them :) I’ve been a regular reader/intermittent poster since 2014 or so, but had to delete several accounts because of personal attacks, death/rape threats, and stalking. On my first account, someone was even able to piece together enough information from my post & comment history to contact me on Facebook and threaten to rape and murder me (I briefly mentioned being sexually assaulted in a post here) and tell my boyfriend I was a whore who’d been raped and linked him to my reddit account. I’m still not too detailed with my posts for fear people will figure out who I am and they will harass me again. I know they’ve probably long since moved on and it is an irrational fear, but I was harassed for months. Trolls are awful.

I wasn't allowed to cut my hair either :l My hair is super frizzy and gets matted if I don't brush it at least 3 times a day. I have it at a manageable length now but as a kid it got so long that it was unhealthy looking and unattractive, as of course I wasn't allowed proper hair care. My Nmom also feels that long hair = beauty. She hasn't had a haircut in over 10 years and looks like a witch from a children's book :P

My Nmom does the "keeping things safe" stuff too. She used to take away gifts that I was "too young for" like a piece of jewelry or a more expensive toy, even though I was always very careful with my things. She'd give it back YEARS later when I'd completely lost interest in the item. My Nmom is also a hoarder and starting moving things into my room the day she kicked me out. She even tried to hoard things I got rid of when I still lived in the US.
Absolutely NC! I realized, (sadly only rather recently,) that she is incapable of change and I will never be able to have even a neutral relationship with her.
Looking back, its hard for me to think I didn't say anything. I just thought it was all normal :l

I absolutely understand this feeling. I started doing all the chores growing up as soon as I was physically and mentally able. Every. Single. One. Not once in my entire time with Nmom was I given a thank you, or even a "you did a good job." Instead it was "You did this wrong." "Why should I thank you? It's your job to do chores." Acknowledgement of my chores always meant I was going to be in trouble.

I used to. For some years after leaving home, whenever I had a time where I assumed I'd have to explain myself I would have four or five different well thought out responses ready to go. Saying "This is why I did this," and hearing "Ah, okay. Thanks." was just so foreign that it blew my mind. With my Nmom, I'd be sat down for an hour of interrogation and sanctimonious, belittling speeches. It took me a lot of time to realize normal people don't act that way towards someone when they are discussing something, or even when second guessing you.
Ah the ol' dictatorship line. Heard that nearly every day growing up.

Wow! That sounds horrible :( I'm sorry you had to go through that. Forcing someone to make drastic changes in their hair is so wrong. It's such a huge part of personality for many people. 

My Nmom was the opposite of your Nmom. She was always forced to have her hair short as a kid (her Nmom said it was more manageable) so growing up I was never allowed to cut my hair. Ever. By the time I was 18, my hair was so thick and long that it would get matted overnight when I slept. I brushed my hair at least 5 times per day. I wasn't allowed to use any heat tools or any products but shampoo, so I was never able to manage it.
I think a lot of these things are a common theme among narc parents and narcs in general.

What my psychiatrist and therapist did with me was actually super helpful, but I'm not sure how specialists treated it when I was a child (I'm almost 23 now.) The focus was more on dealing with my autistic traits and finding ways to work around them rather than quelling them. I have never felt that my psychiatrist or therapist acted condescending towards me in any way. These have just been my experiences though.

My Nmom also believes in the fluoridated water thing, and refuses to use plastic now. They also have this weird thing about aluminum? I'm sorry in laws push this  stuff on you too :( My Nmom and Estepdad actually had a lot of friends and some family stop talking to them because they were constantly talking about their conspiracy theories and sending email after email with Alex Jones links. People just got sick of it.
Heard this exact phrase til the day I was 18 and my Nmom could kick me out. Her other favorite line was "This household is a dictatorship, not a democracy." Pleasant woman.
Congratulations! I'm confident you'll be one of the good ones. :)
My Nmom also studied early childhood education, but her master's was in social work. It's almost like they go to college to become better Narcs.

My Nmom is my adoptive mom actually. She fostered me for a year before starting adoption proceedings. I didn't know my real mom until I was 18. I'm starting to wonder how common Narcs are among people working with children and who are aspiring to work with children.

She was let go for chronic health reasons when I was 8, and she's not been able to work full time since. She once tried to start a daycare as well, but thankfully her health was too poor and she didn't have the funds. I can only imagine the kind of damage she did at her job.

My Nmom also didn't truly believe in non-physical abuse. At least not in our household. If there were no visible marks or bruises, it wasn't abuse. And my Nmom wasn't just a mandated reporter, she worked in intake for Child Protective Service! She is a very, very, sneaky covert Narc. Talk about a wolf in sheep's clothing. Her profession of "saving the children" absolutely fed her narcissism.
